name: alakazam_ml_v29
model: A LightGBM LambdaRank policy learned from frozen top-Alakazam public replays. It ranks every legal MAIN action using board, ordered bench, option-set, v28 policy, and inherited-ranker features.
model_scope: The learned policy controls single-choice MAIN context decisions. v28 remains the fallback for nested selections, low confidence, unsupported contexts, time pressure, and deterministic safety routes.

teacher_training.label: All legal options with the teacher's card or attack and target state are positive, collapsing duplicate copies.
teacher_training.episode_split: 70% train, 10% validation, 20% test by replay hash

frozen_corpus_runtime_regression.note: This is an in-sample regression check over the frozen top-five corpus, not an unbiased generalization estimate.

safety_guards: Always preserve a deterministic immediate lethal attack.
Do not replace a complete fallback Boss route with a non-Boss MAIN action.
Reject candidates that destroy a currently available KO.
Never end the turn while the Active Alakazam can attack.
Do not cycle Dudunsparce away from a board of two or fewer Pokemon.
Use v28 for unsupported, nested, multi-select, low-time, or illegal cases.
known_limitations: The requested 90% top-choice agreement was not reached on unseen episodes: held-out semantic top-1 is 66.30%. Top-3 recall is 90.95%.
The 84.82% frozen-corpus runtime result includes training episodes and must not be read as a held-out estimate.
The learned model currently covers MAIN context only; nested choices still use the v28 deterministic policy.
Local arena results are opponent- and seed-dependent. Across two recorded seeds, Grimmsnarl improved while generic Mega Starmie was mixed.
A real leaderboard submission is required to determine whether v29 improves the approximately 800 rating.
